headline: Continued fueling station, parking, and subdivision applications at South Willow Street to July 16, 2026; Pearl Street Garage brought back for compliance hearing.
summary: Several applications were continued to later dates, including projects at 1279 South Willow Street, 1265 South Willow Street, and Wellington Road. Members found five new applications complete and set them for public hearing. The Pearl Street Garage applicant will return for a compliance hearing on design changes.
decisions: Continued the Wellington Road subdivision application (S2026-005) to August 5, 2026.
Continued the charitable gaming facility site plan at 1279 South Willow Street (SP2026-010) to July 16, 2026.
Continued the parking reduction permit at 1279 South Willow Street (CU2026-004) to July 16, 2026.
Continued the lot line adjustment for 1265 South Willow Street and 55 John E. Devine Drive (S2026-011) to July 16, 2026.
Continued the fueling station site plan at 1265 South Willow Street (SP2026-011) to July 16, 2026.
Continued the parking reduction permit at 1265 South Willow Street (CU2026-005) to July 16, 2026.
Approved finding that the conditional use application for 285 Manchester Street (CU2026-007) is complete and setting a public hearing.
Approved finding that applications SP2026-013, S2026-013, S2026-014, and SP2026-012 are complete and setting public hearings.
No action taken on the request to postpone the completeness decision for the 103 Ray Street subdivision; it was placed on the July 16th agenda because there was no quorum.
Approved bringing the Pearl Street Garage applicant back for a compliance hearing on design changes.
Approved the minutes of June 4, 2026 as written, with two abstentions.

2. New Item SP2026-013 155 
 Property located at 231 Woodland Avenue (Tax Map 490, Lots 18 & 18A), a site plan 156 
 application for a change in use from an existing food processing plant to a landscape 157

 improvements, in an R-1B Zoning District. Keach-Nordstrom Associates, Inc. for 159 
 Greywacke, LLC. (Reviewed under Current Zoning Ordinance) 160 
 161 
Matt Peterson, Keach-Nordstrom Associates, was present, along with the property owner.  162 
Mr. Peterson explained that this is a proposed change of use application regarding the 163 
property at 231 Woodland Ave. The site in question is located about ¾ of the way down 164 
Woodland Ave. on the left side. It is a standalone industrial building that, based on the 165 
tax card, was built around 1960. In 1994, this site was given Site Plan approval from the 166 
Planning Board for a one-story machine shop. The uses have changed over time. It was a 167 
food processing site for some time and there were complaints of animals using the 168 
dumpster, with food not being disposed of properly. The proposed use does not include 169 
any of that type of negativity.  170 
 171 
Mr. Peterson explained that there are currently three parcels: Lot 18 is approximately 172 
0.287 acres; Lot 18A is approximately 0.25 acres; and Castle Street, a paper street, is 173 
being added to the parcel at approximately 0.067 acres, for a total of 0.604 acres or 174 
26,308 s.f. The attorneys are working on the mergers and the paper street's quiet title 175 
currently. Any approval would have to be conditioned upon these items being completed.  176 
 177 
Currently, there is an approximately 6,000 s.f. building on the site, along with an outside 178 
storage area. There is an open curb cut all the way down the street, and the site is mostly 179 
paved.  The proposed demolition plans show some areas of pavement to be removed. 180
Manchester Planning Board 
Public Hearing Meeting   Page 5 of 18 
July 2, 2026 
 
Currently, the pavement bleeds over into the legitimate paper street area. This pavement 181 
will be removed and brought into compliance with the Site Plan. There are a couple other 182 
areas of pavement to be cleaned up as well. The Site Plan shows curbing to make the site 183 
conducive to DPW, EPD, and Planning Board requirements. Instead of a wide open curb 184 
cut, the applicant is proposing a landscape area. The area along Woodland Ave. will be 185 
very similar to front yards which lead down the road. The DPW will plow that area, as 186 
they do now. The closed curb cut area will be more defined for this plowing. In the past, 187 
people pulled up to the front of the building and backed into Woodland Ave. The 188 
intention is to minimize this circulation from a safety standpoint by cleaning up the open 189 
curb cut along the whole frontage.  190 
 191 
Mr. Peterson explained that the Site Plan proposes an 8’ fence for which a variance has 192 
been obtained. This will start with a gate at a location as proposed to the Zoning Board. 193 
An abutter has a shed on their property near this location, and the Zoning Board asked the 194 
applicant to move the gate back to allow the abutter access to the shed. The abutter does 195 
not have any easements across the applicant’s property for this, but the applicant worked 196 
to allow this access by moving the fence away from the property line. Four parking 197 
spaces are proposed in the front on the site. The proposal is a change of use to a 198 
landscape business. This is not a typical landscape business including selling mulch and 199 
retail items. The owner owns a landscape business in Massachusetts which has run out of 200 
space. The site in question allows the owner the opportunity to store his vehicles on the 201 
site, in order for employees to pick up their landscape trucks and equipment on the way 202 
to their jobs. It is not envisioned that many other people will come to the site to buy 203 
anything. No material will be stored on site. It was mentioned to the Zoning Board that 204 
workers may come back with mulch on their trucks and dump it in a pile at the back of 205 
the site while cleaning the trucks. This material is not for display or sale. The four 206 
parking spaces are proposed for the small office use of the business. There may be 1-2 207 
people at a time working from the office. There will be space at the back of the site for all 208 
of the employee trucks. A ramp is proposed into the building to allow for access and a 209 
place to put the vehicles and equipment inside the building for protection.  210 
 211 
Mr. Peterson stated that the owner has met with abutters before coming to the Board. The 212 
applicant is proposing a sidewalk of raised concrete without any curbing. Part of the 213 
variances received from the Zoning Board include items for landscaping. However, there 214 
are other items within the Site Plan regulations which were discovered and a waiver has 215 
been requested. The applicant is proposing 15 shrubs along the front of the site, with 216 
landscaping in the right of way, and shrubs on the property itself. The goal is to beautify 217 
the streetscape. A landscaping plan and a lighting plan were submitted. Three wall packs 218 
are shown on the site. A company from Hampton, NH is used for the lights and the 219 
lighting will be dark sky compliant. The wall packs will be as shown on the plan, with 220 
downcast lighting around the perimeter for employees accessing the site. The waiver 221 
request is from basic submission material, Section E, requiring a stamp from a landscape 222 
architect. This is requested as there are only 15 shrubs being proposed.  223

3. New Item S2026-013 327 
 Property located at 111 Villa Street (Tax Map 365, Lot 30), an application to subdivide 328 
 an existing parcel of 13,555 SF into two lots of 7,284 SF (Lot 30) and 6,271 SF (Lot 329 
 30A), where an existing two-family home is to remain on Lot 30 and a new single- or 330 
 two-family house is to be constructed on Lot 30A in a Residential Two-Family (R-2) 331 
 Zoning District. Joseph Wichert, LLS, Inc. for David and Gail Cote. (Reviewed under 332

Joe Wichert, Joseph Wichert, LLS, Inc., was present for David and Gail Cote, and 335 
explained that this lot is located on the south side of Villa St. The existing house is 336 
situated on the west side of the lot and is a two-story, two-family dwelling. The proposal 337 
is to create one new R-2 building lot. A variance was required and obtained for this 338 
application. The requirement is 60’ of frontage and 100’ depth. A variance was needed 339 
because the parent parcel was less than 100’ deep. The lot is 92.8’ on the east side and 340 
95.5’ on the west side. The proposal is to create one lot with 67’ of frontage and 6,271 341 
s.f. of area. In order to accomplish this, a small bump out that was built onto the garage 342 
will be removed and some pavement on the east side of the lot will be eliminated. The 343 
intention is for the owners to build a new house on the new lot and one of their children 344 
to move into the two-family. The DPW had comments regarding some existing trees on 345 
the lot which are very tight to the edge of pavement and are not in great condition. The 346 
application includes removal of those trees. It is unclear if this will be an issue with 347 
DPW. He noted that he was told these trees have been hit by the plow because they sit so 348 
tight to the road. There are not final building plans yet but there is a fairly large tree 349 
canopy. The applicant is willing to install a street tree if needed to replace the trees 350 
proposed to be removed. The  existing house and new lot will be serviced by municipal 351 
sewer and water.  352 
 353

 355 
 Ms. Baldwin stated that it appears there are mature trees in the back of the lot as well. 356 
 She asked if these would be on the new lot and preserved. Mr. Wichert stated that he did 357 
 not locate all trees on the lot, and he believes this tree is still in place. The applicant may 358 
 need to remove that tree during construction and does not want to be restricted from 359

 removal. The applicant believes that the trees along the road will need to be removed and 360

 362 
Alderman Kaw-uh asked if the Board is restricted in terms of the caliper of tree that can 363 
be required for replanting. Ms. Bixby stated that the SubSite regulations have a standard 364 
of 3’ for street trees at time of planting. The standard for on-site shade trees is 3.5’ at time 365

one at the back of the property, the Board could consider larger trees. Ms. Strong stated 367 
that the Board should likely stay within what the SubSite regulations indicate, unless the 368 
applicant is agreeable to something larger. The Chair stated that he would like a condition 369 
that, if the trees along the road are removed, they should be replaced with a street tree. He 370 
is otherwise okay with sticking to the SubSite standards for replanting. 371 
 372 
 Mr. Wichert asked if the Board is discussing the tree located in the back yard. The Chair 373 
 stated that he was not speaking of this tree specifically. Alderman Kaw-uh stated that he 374 
 was not speaking of that tree either. He noted that the owner would likely want to 375 
 preserve a large shade tree on the property, if possible. He was concerned with the street 376 
 trees. Mr. Wichert noted that applicants have the right to cut trees on their own property. 377 
 He could instruct applicants to cut trees potentially proposed to be removed prior to the 378 
 Board hearing. If someone is building on a property, they generally want nice amenities 379 
 such as shade trees, but replacement of trees at the applicant’s cost adds up. An applicant 380

 charged with making sure the City aesthetics remain pleasant and improved. If it is within 383 
 the jurisdiction of the Board to require a tree replanting, the pleasure of an applicant is 384 
 not reason to forgo this, if in the best interest of the City.  385
